title: Cluster Upgrade Phased Rollout — Cost Exposure Lens & Emergency Abort Flow
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Problem: Operators managing Private/VPC clusters need a quick way to evaluate the downstream cost exposure and service impact of a phased cluster upgrade before starting a rollout, and a clearly visible emergency abort flow when a canary or early cohort shows degradation. Current console surfaces silo metrics (latency, error rate, token spend) but lacks a single compact lens that ties projected token-cost delta to rollout cohorts and exposes an action-safe abort/rollback path.

Goal: Design a compact ‘Cost Exposure Lens’ that sits on the rollout details page and surfaces: estimated token cost delta (per-hour / per-day / per-tenant), cohort-level latency & error sensors, confidence markers, and a one-click abort path with guarded confirmation and telemetry capture. Deliver high-fidelity desktop and compact mobile/ops panel prototypes, interaction specs for engineers, and a short usability script for 5-run participant sessions.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype for desktop rollout details including Cost Exposure Lens and abort modal
Compact/compact-ops responsive variants that render in the tenant-ops inspector panel
Interaction spec covering hover explanations, confidence thresholds, and abort confirmation states
Usability test plan + script and recruitment criteria for 5 platform operators
Sign-off from PM (Maya Chen) and Eng lead (Ravi Patel) on telemetry fields and abort semantics
design_notes: Lens should compute cost exposure using active token rate * delta model variant cost, with a 24h and 7d rolling view
Show cohort-level stacked sparkbars for latency/error and an overlayed cost delta ribbon
Make abort flow explicit: 2-step modal, require typed confirmation for production cohorts, include optional incident template to capture operator notes
Trade-off: preferring clarity over micro-optimizations in first iteration; complex caching delta calculations will be surfaced as telemetry tags rather than inline formulas
Accessibility: ensure colorblind-friendly palette and keyboard-first abort confirmation
